dissent: Pickup may optimize price checking while missing the actual job: couples might want an affordable evening out, not food to carry home. Even unprompted reopening could reflect curiosity rather than a dinner decision; do not interpret the proposed pilot as purchase or willingness-to-pay evidence.

say: Research interpretation (unproven): The strongest receipt establishes municipal cleanup at Māras pond—both a relevant problem and an existing alternative—not demand for verified missions. Compare Pond Patrol with municipal cleanup and ordinary self-directed safe litter picking; the latter needs no reporting or checker. Acquisition through SSE Sustainability is only a proposed channel: permission, eligible reach and recruitment effort are unknown. uncertainty: Verified missions offer enough convenience or motivation to outweigh reporting, claiming and evidence submission.
Ten eligible regular walkers can be reached through the proposed student channel without excessive recruitment effort; this sample would not establish wider acquisition viability.
Safe actionable litter recurs frequently enough after municipal cleanup to support repeat participation.
Existing approved tools have no incremental charge. Payment-link capability and card pricing establish neither willingness to pay nor a sustainable payer.
Channel permission, invitation-to-enrollment conversion, refusals and acquisition minutes per enrolled and returning walker.
dissent: A free civic experiment can be worthwhile without positive commercial margin, provided its subsidy and volunteer workload are explicit.
Municipal cleanup could complement walkers rather than eliminate the need; one cleanup receipt cannot settle recurrence.
Failure caused by an empty safe-mission list disproves this pond's proposed daily loop more directly than walker motivation. Do not manufacture tasks or replace dropouts to rescue the threshold.
